newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC, Zurich merge language units.
newsitem.headline: SBC, Zurich merge language units.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) and insurer Zurich Group said they had merged their language units in a new company specialised in language and translation services for Switzerland's large financial sector.
The new company, named CLS Corporate Language Services AG, is two-thirds owned by SBC and one-third by Zurich's domestic arm, Zurich Switzerland.
SBC, Switzerland's third-biggest bank, and Zurich, the biggest Swiss direct insurer, already cooperate in cross-selling bank and life insurance products in Switzerland.
CLS has a workforce of 40 drawn from the two in-house language units, which have also been active on the external market, SBC and Zurich said in a joint statement.
"There is no language company specialised in the financial sector in Switzerland that is a big as we are," managing director Doris Marty-Albisser told Reuters.
Other verbal and text translation services were much smaller and worked heavily with freelancers, she said.
CLS will offer translation and editorial services as well as consulting on the use of information technology for language work, translation and vocabulary databases.
"We will cover the Swiss market and accept orders from abroad. An expansion abroad is under review," Marty-Albisser said.
CLS offices will be in Basle, Zurich, Lausanne and Chiasso. Switzerland has four national languages -- German, French, Italian and Romansch -- and English is also widely used in the financial sector.
